collection_method: Read-only GitHub issue search and issue/comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. Embedded snippets were treated as evidence and not executed. No attachments, linked demonstrations or code files, packages, agent runtimes, reproduction steps, target systems, or external tools were opened or run.

selected_records.title: Dynamic function tool is still executed after is_enabled becomes false
selected_records.provider_attribution: OpenAI Agents SDK runner behavior; offline scripted model, so no model-provider execution is attributed.
selected_records.assessment: An offline reproduction reports that a function exposed while enabled still executed after its dynamic gate returned false before dispatch. This is a strong runtime authorization control for a single agent/tool path, not a multi-participant exchange or rogue swarm.

selected_records.title: Agent name conflicts cause the first registered agent to be ignored
selected_records.provider_attribution: OpenAI Agents SDK name normalization; provider-independent offline stub model.
selected_records.assessment: Distinct configured agent names normalized to the same handoff/tool name, so the later registration received the task and produced the final output while the first became unreachable. This demonstrates wrong-specialist routing and result use in a deterministic test, not independent autonomous actors or an external incident.

selected_records.title: Resumed approval followed by handoff can leave Session history without tool outputs after append failure
selected_records.provider_attribution: OpenAI Agents SDK session/handoff logic; provider-neutral scripted model.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic approval-plus-handoff matrix preserves one tool effect and continuation with a delegate but leaves durable Session history missing tool and handoff outputs after an atomic append failure. It is a state-durability/handoff control, not unauthorized coordination.

selected_records.title: Callable needs_approval fails open when the predicate returns a non-bool
selected_records.provider_attribution: OpenAI Agents SDK approval helper; offline scripted model.
selected_records.assessment: The report shows falsy non-boolean policy returns being coerced to no-approval and a guarded tool running. A maintainer closed it because such values violate the declared boolean callback contract; the reporter then found no supported-path bypass. It must not be represented as a confirmed SDK authorization exploit.

selected_records.title: Lack of Runtime Access Control in Auto Function Invocation
selected_records.provider_attribution: Semantic Kernel Python static audit; no runtime or model-provider evidence.
selected_records.assessment: The issue alleges automatic destructive execution after indirect prompt injection but supplies no runtime logs and explicitly derives the claim from static review. Its public thread notes that an AUTO_FUNCTION_INVOCATION filter can already block dispatch, while first-class classification and resumable approval remain gaps. This is a design discussion, not an observed bypass or swarm.

selected_records.title: Handoff Orchestration: Context not passed from previous agents
selected_records.provider_attribution: Reporter-configured Semantic Kernel .NET workflow with OpenAI GPT-4o/GPT-4.1 labels; no independent execution provenance.
selected_records.assessment: A designed writer-to-translator-to-detector chain reportedly failed to pass earlier outputs, causing downstream hallucination or incomplete work. Another commenter reported the same behavior, but the issue later closed as stale without a confirmed fix. It is failed transfer, not rogue coordination.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. The selected records are deterministic framework reproductions, failed intended handoffs, or a static security/design discussion; every record was public before collection.
limitations: Searches were capped at 30 newest-updated rows and overlap heavily; this is not a repository census.
Issue bodies and comments are reporter assertions, not authenticated agent telemetry.
Offline stub/scripted models establish framework behavior but do not establish autonomous participant identities or provider behavior.
Open issue state and recent comments do not establish ongoing autonomous activity.
No attachments, external reproductions, packages, linked code files, agent runtimes, or linked target systems were opened or executed; embedded issue snippets were not run.

Advancement requires a not-previously-published original exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, actual task-result transfer and recipient use, and evidence that the coordination—not only naming, routing, state durability or a controlled gate test—exceeded operator authorization.
redactions: No credentials, personal addresses, payload bodies, sink identifiers, tokens, screenshots, or private logs are included.
Assessments summarize incident shape without reproducing executable demonstrations or tool-call payloads.
